description: Predict the next minute of lubricant-temperature change from measured friction power and thermal boundaries. A thermal resistance network competes with a speed-dependent mixing hypothesis; no future control measurements are inputs.
display_title: Frictional heating in a robot gearbox

assumptions: Lumped thermal balance with measured instantaneous torque and speed
Housing, environment and friction power are held locally constant over 60 seconds; later controls are never supplied
Capacity and conductances are effective quantities; one joint, no independent-machine validation
equation_templates.name: Friction-heated thermal resistance network

nodes.meaning: Instantaneous frictional mechanical power available as heat
Heat flow to the measured housing
Direct effective heat flow to the measured environment
Net instantaneous power into the lubricant thermal store
Exact relaxation fraction for a locally constant thermal boundary
Predicted lubricant temperature change over the next minute

capacity.meaning: Effective lubricant thermal capacity under the measured torque-power convention

preprocessing.native_reading: Deterministic coordinate and SI conversions; source-derived responses explicitly identified

scientific_scope: Constitutive hypotheses and matched predictive tests; no novelty, causality or independent discovery claim
split_policy: Source identification runs train except 1.4137 rad/s dev; every source validation run is test. Nonoverlapping 60-second windows; instantaneous start-state inputs only. Single robot joint.

stability.domain: Native measured domain; bounded perturbations of continuous inputs only
stability.scope: Diagnostic sensitivity; source-calibrated measurement-error distributions unavailable
